body:
how does a song nobody released as a single, one that fell to no. 71 and then off the chart, come back four years later and go no. 1? the eras tour opened with it nightly until fans caught up. fifth-longest climb in hot 100 history.

longlivets.com/?era=lover&utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=era-deep-cut
why: Calendar slot 2026-08-13 23:30Z X, heartbeat:era-deep-cut on lover, hook "an honest question" — and deliberately a different subject from the 23:00Z Decode post, per the strategy’s no-sibling rule on heartbeat days. Every claim traces to the Vault Lover item "Cruel Summer takes four years to become a No. 1" (sourced Billboard + Rolling Stone): never a single, the fall to No. 71 and off the chart, the Eras Tour Lover-set nightly opener and the fan groundswell, No. 1 on the chart dated Oct. 28, 2023, and the fifth-longest climb to No. 1 in Hot 100 history. Lover also appears on 08-16 (on-this-day, the title-track waltz) — three days apart, different pillar, different subject; flagged here so it is a visible choice rather than drift. Trimmed to weighted ≤270 per X length rule. | 2026-08-12 Taylor-photo standard (issue #2031, Joey directive): attached a real credited photograph of Taylor from the repo corpus (apps/web/lib/longlive/lenses.ts), rehosted under /social/library/photos/. Campaign renamed to a STORY-UNIQUE value: findPostedDuplicate treats same platform+campaign as an already-posted duplicate, so the old thematic bucket campaigns (heartbeat:*) would have false-skipped every post in a bucket after its first one landed. Visible credit line omitted from the body only because it would exceed X’s 280 weighted chars; the credit is recorded in mediaCredit.
